title: Certificate and apex DNS cutover for chattic.us

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Cutover is DNS: move the apex A/AAAA records for chattic.us from the product
CloudFront distribution to the marketing one, once story 1 (chatticus-a9fc83)
and story 3 (chatticus-ef8371) are verified green against the marketing
distribution's own CloudFront domain. Do this after task 12
(chatticus-cd78ca) removes marketing routes from the product web app, so
there is no window where both distributions claim to serve chattic.us with
different content.

dev.chattic.us and staging.chattic.us are unaffected — marketing is production
only.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Cutover executed. Sequence: (1) merged and promoted the product-repo changes dropping WEB_MARKETING_DOMAINS and the marketing alias/host-routing/apex-records from ChatticusWeb* (PR #298); (2) waited for the production deploy (ChatticusWebProduction) to succeed, confirming it released the chattic.us alias; (3) immediately pushed the marketing repo's CHATTICUS_MARKETING_INCLUDE_APEX=1 change, triggering ChatticusMarketing to claim the apex.

Actual downtime window: chattic.us was unreachable from when ChatticusWebProduction's deploy completed until ChatticusMarketing's deploy completed and the new distribution's alias propagated -- roughly the two deploy durations back to back (a few minutes), not the CloudFront propagation delay itself since DNS never had to change (both distributions' apex A/AAAA records point at whichever CloudFront distribution currently holds the alias in AWS's global anycast layer, not a Route53 change). hey.chattic.us, dev.chattic.us, and staging.chattic.us were unaffected throughout, confirmed by curl during the window.

One operational hiccup, unrelated to the cutover logic itself: the #297 and #298 merges landed close enough together that their two 'Deploy Web (development)'/'Deploy ThinTurn (development)' CI runs raced against the same CloudFormation stack; the second of each failed with UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS/CREATE_IN_PROGRESS conflicts rather than queuing. Both re-triggered manually and succeeded on retry -- dev.chattic.us's root was briefly still showing marketing content until the retry landed, now fixed.

Final verification: chattic.us and www.chattic.us serve the marketing site (/, /beta/, /contact/services/, /wiki/ all 200; /api/waitlist/survey 200 through the same-origin proxy). hey.chattic.us, dev.chattic.us, and staging.chattic.us all serve the workspace at root (title check on all three).
